tools.name: minerva_pcb_move_component
tools.description: Move a component to an absolute position. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors and component names from minerva_pcb_get_components. FREEFORM (HITL-6): snap_to_grid:false lands the part exactly where asked, no grid — align a pad row with another part's off-grid row so a 2-pin span routes with ZERO bends. On success the reply may carry dangling_copper: committed trace endpoints that sat on this component's (or its group members') pads before the move and now touch none of them [{trace_id, net, at:[x,y], component_id, message}] — copper does not follow parts; delete (minerva_pcb_delete_traces) or reroute those traces before routing new work.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry
tools.description: Export routed traces and vias from a PCB editor. Returns trace data in the same format accepted by import_trace_geometry, enabling round-trip workflows. Every segment carries the trace_id of the trace it belongs to (the segments of one polyline trace all repeat the SAME trace_id — that is how you tell which segments are one piece of copper). Vias carry an id key when they have an identity, which is every via created through the editor or through import; the key is ABSENT on a via restored from a board file predating stable via ids, and such a via cannot be addressed by minerva_pcb_delete_traces. Use these ids with minerva_pcb_delete_traces to remove a subset, or feed them back through import_trace_geometry to keep identities stable across a round trip.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_delete_traces
tools.description: Delete a SUBSET of committed traces and vias by identity, without touching the rest of the board. Use this instead of exporting everything, filtering, and re-importing (import_trace_geometry clears the whole board first). Get the ids from minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry, which stamps a trace_id on every segment and an id on every via. AT LEAST ONE of trace_ids, via_ids or net_name is REQUIRED — a call with none of them is an error, because deleting nothing and deleting everything must never be the same request. An EMPTY net_name (or empty id arrays) does not count as supplying a selector, so a call carrying only net_name:"" is that same error rather than a no-op. Selection is by identity ONLY — trace_ids, via_ids and net_name are combined as a union, and a trace named by both trace_ids and net_name is deleted and counted exactly once — and there is deliberately no region/bounding-box selector: to clear traces in an area, export, filter on the real coordinates yourself, then name the ids you chose. net_name selects traces only, never vias; name a via by id to remove it. Partial-trace clipping (splitting a trace at a boundary) is not supported — a trace is deleted whole or not at all. Naming an id that does not exist is NOT an error: the ids that do exist are deleted and the stale ones come back in missing_trace_ids/missing_via_ids. An EMPTY-string id is reported there too rather than skipped — that is what you get from an item predating stable ids, whose id key the export omits entirely. Those two keys are present only when you supplied the corresponding selector, so an empty array means 'checked, none stale' while an absent key means 'you named none'. Undoable in one step via the board's normal undo.

via_ids.description: Exact via ids to delete (as returned in each via's id by export_trace_geometry)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints
tools.description: Route the board's open route hints and either PROPOSE routes (default) or COMMIT them as real traces. Default (commit absent/false): runs the router over the selected open route hints and lands the results as RouteCandidates in the panel's routing workspace (no annotation is written; the board is not mutated) — resolve a candidate via minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/_reject(candidate_id), or minerva_pcb_workspace_list/get_active to inspect it first. Set commit=true to materialize the routed polylines as real traces in the board model (journaled) and transition the source hints open→applied. Partial/failed routing returns WHERE it got stuck (unrouted nets with their blocked pad pairs) as structured feedback, and every routing reply carries board_health (DCR 019fd5fd9084): whole-board completeness + assembly advisory, enriched panel-side with board_revision and preflight.rendered_this_revision. ISLAND DELTA (UX2 station 6): island_deltas?:[{net, pin_groups_before, pin_groups_after, hint_ids?}] reports what each route BUYS against the pre-proposal census — e.g. 9 pin groups -> 8 means this candidate merges two islands; a delta of zero on a partial net means the new copper connects nothing new. ROUTE QUALITY (Epoch UX2 station 4 + HITL-6): every candidate record carries bend_count and routed_length_mm (zeros for a vias-only candidate), plus length_ratio (routed / per-run manhattan minimum, approximate; absent when that minimum is ~0) and, on single-run candidates, misalignment_mm — the perpendicular offset between the span's endpoints (min(|dx|,|dy|)). THE 2-PIN RULE: on a two-pin span, ANY bend means the pads do not align — length_ratio 1.0 only says the detour is efficient, never that it is necessary; misalignment_mm > 0 says the PLACEMENT is the thing to fix (align with minerva_pcb_move_component snap_to_grid:false, then re-propose) — weigh that before committing. A high ratio or bend count on a longer hop is the same smell at larger scale. Iterate: edit/add hints and re-run; applied hints are excluded by default so only fresh open hints re-route. LEGACY MIGRATION (Epoch UX1 station 12, DCR 019fd095e694): a selected non-'detailed' hint carrying inline waypoints whose task has no routing_constraint yet has that corridor seeded ONCE into a durable task constraint (authored_by "migration") before routing runs, and the hint's waypoints are then marked superseded and refuse further edits.

commit.description: false/absent (default): land RouteCandidates in the routing workspace only, board unchanged. true: materialize routed traces + mark source hints applied.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_hint_convert_to_detailed
tools.description: Convert a SUPERSEDED guided route hint to 'detailed', reclaiming manual waypoint control. A legacy guided hint whose inline waypoints were seeded into a task-level routing constraint (marked kind_payload.waypoints_superseded_by_constraint_revision — the station-12 migration, or a live steer) has inert waypoints: the host refuses waypoint edits and routing reads only the constraint. This named operation clears that task constraint (only when this hint singly owns it), then strips the supersession marker and the offline lock fields and sets detail_level='detailed' — ordered two-store writes, NOT a spanning transaction: a torn save is repaired by deterministic load-time reconciliation, and undo restores the annotation side only (one history step; re-run this tool to complete a half-undone conversion) — afterwards the hint's waypoints are editable again, routing follows them literally (as-drawn) on the next propose, and the hint is never re-seeded. Use it when an edit was refused with error 'waypoints_superseded' (or offline with 'live_editor_required') and you want to hand-edit the path instead of steering the constraint. Refuses by name: constraint_not_singly_owned when a merged multi-hint task owns the constraint (converting would orphan shared steering — steer via minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route instead), not_superseded for an ordinary unstamped hint, hint_not_found / not_a_route_hint otherwise.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_via
tools.description: Manually insert a via on a pcb_route_hint proposal (a route carrying kind_payload.segments): splits the segment nearest board point (x, y) into two at the projected point, appends a via there, and recomputes every segment's copper layer via the layer-run toggle (F.Cu<->B.Cu at each via position, in path order) — the same split+via+layer-run geometry the canvas Add-Via tool uses, so an agent's call and a human's click produce identical results. Use this to resolve a routing collision by hand when the autorouter's own vias-avoidance left a proposal single-layer through an obstacle: one via jumps the trace to the opposite layer past that point, a second via jumps it back. No-op (error) if (x, y) is not near any segment. Persists through the host's revision-history seam, so minerva_pcb_hint_undo/minerva_pcb_hint_redo cover it.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_load_board
tools.description: Load a complete PCB board from canonical YAML into the editor in ONE call — components (with pins and pad geometry), nets, traces, vias, and mounting holes. This is the whole-board importer; it replaces the multi-call add_component / connect_net / import_footprint_geometry / import_trace_geometry sequence. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `path` (absolute file path, read server-side — PREFER THIS for files on disk: it costs ~20 tokens instead of the whole board twice) or `yaml` (inline canonical board source, for boards you authored in-context). The canonical contract: width_mm/height_mm, components[].ref whose pins carry pad geometry via drill_mm/annulus_diameter_mm for through-hole or pad_width_mm/pad_height_mm for SMD, plus nets, traces, vias, mounting_holes. Returns component_count, net_count, deserialize warnings, board_name, and source_digest (sha256 of the loaded YAML text — compare it to verify the board that landed is byte-identical to your source). DESTRUCTIVE REPLACE with an honesty report: loading swaps the WHOLE live board, and the reply's `delta` field names what the incoming source lacked relative to the live board it replaced (components_removed, traces_reduced per net, vias_removed, zones/cutouts/mounting_holes_removed, plus `dropped` sentences). READ IT — a source missing entities the live board had (e.g. a YAML with no zones) destroys them; reconciliation is the CALLER's judgment, this tool only reports. SIDECAR ADOPTION (Epoch UX2 station 8): the `path` form adopts the file as the panel's document path — annotations become durable-by-default (<path>.annotations.json auto-written debounced on every mutation), an existing sidecar (annotations + routing workspace) is restored on load, and the reply says so: annotations_sidecar:"adopted" + annotations_restored (count, when a sidecar was read). The inline `yaml` form adopts nothing. BOARD HEALTH AT LOAD (UX2 station 9): the reply carries `board_health` — the same whole-board ledger a route reply carries (completeness census: complete/missing_copper/partial/indeterminate, + tri-state assembly, panel-enriched with board_revision/preflight) — computed at open with NO routing run, so "8 nets unrouted, GND in 9 islands" is known before the first verb; the established `assembly` key remains.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_propose_zone
tools.description: STAGE a zone (copper pour or keepout) as a DRAFT — the staging family's twin of minerva_pcb_create_zone (same args, same validation, same refusal texts), landing a review ghost instead of writing the board. FAMILY NOTE: propose_* tools STAGE BOARD ENTITIES; the unrelated workspace_propose_* tools run the ROUTER. Nothing is journalled and nothing appears on the board until minerva_pcb_staged_accept; the ghost persists via the routing sidecar without an explicit save. A staged keepout also detours DRAFT route proposals (the composed request). Reply: {entity_id, staged_id, kind, net, layer, point_count}.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

net.description: Declared net name. Required for a copper pour; optional for a keepout.

outline.description: Outline points in board mm, in order. At least 3 required.

note.description: Optional human-readable rationale stored on the draft

tools.name: minerva_pcb_propose_cutout
tools.description: STAGE a cutout (an opening through the whole board) as a DRAFT — the staging family's twin of minerva_pcb_create_cutout (same args, same validation), landing a review ghost instead of writing the board. FAMILY NOTE: propose_* tools STAGE BOARD ENTITIES; the unrelated workspace_propose_* tools run the ROUTER. Nothing lands until minerva_pcb_staged_accept. A staged cutout's whole v1 power is review-before-land (ghost + accept/reject + persistence): like a REAL cutout it is authorable, not compilable, and it never enters a route request. Reply: {entity_id, staged_id, point_count}.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

outline.description: Outline points in board mm, in order. At least 3 required.

note.description: Optional human-readable rationale stored on the draft

tools.name: minerva_pcb_staged_list
tools.description: List staged entity DRAFTS (the staging family — see minerva_pcb_propose_zone). Read-only. By default only LIVE (disposition "staged") entries; include_terminal:true also returns the accepted/rejected audit trail. Each row: {staged_id, entity_id, kind, disposition, author, base_board_revision, zone_kind?, layer?, net?, note?}. entity_id is the canonical board id the ghost/selection/accept all reference.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_staged_accept
tools.description: ACCEPT staged draft(s) (the staging family): replays the direct create with the STORED payload — same id, byte-identical entity — re-validated against the CURRENT board, so drift since staging (net deleted, layer removed) refuses with the direct verb's own reason and the draft stays live. One journalled history step; undo returns the entity to a ghost. Pass entity_id for one draft, or entity_ids (array) for an ALL-OR-NOTHING batch that lands as ONE undo step (refused whole, per-entity reasons, if any member cannot land).

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

entity_id.description: Canonical id of ONE staged draft (zone:<hex>/cutout:<hex>)

entity_ids.description: Canonical ids for an all-or-nothing batch accept (one history step)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_staged_reject
tools.description: REJECT one staged draft (the staging family): terminal — the ghost disappears, the entry is kept as audit, and the reject is paired with its own history entry, so undo revives the ghost while undoing unrelated edits leaves the rejection standing. Unknown/already-terminal entity_id is an error.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

entity_id.description: Canonical id of the staged draft to reject

tools.name: minerva_pcb_group_components
tools.description: Stamp two or more known components into one persistent group (merging any existing groups among them; Illustrator merge grammar, not nesting). One journalled, undoable step. A selection that is already exactly one flat group is a no-op reply (changed:false) with that group's own id/members, not an error. Refused (as an error) when fewer than two known components remain after expansion. Reply: {group_id, member_ids, changed}. Agrees with minerva_pcb_get_components' group_id/group_members fields by construction.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

component_ids.description: Component ids to group (two or more after expansion to existing group-mates)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_ungroup
tools.description: Dissolve the group(s) touched by group_id or component_ids. Positions are untouched — members simply become independently selectable/movable again. One journalled, undoable step when anything is released; releasing nothing (already ungrouped) is a no-op reply (changed:false), not an error. group_id takes precedence when both are given; an unknown group_id, or component_ids naming no known component, is an error.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

group_id.description: Group id to dissolve (takes precedence over component_ids)

component_ids.description: Component ids whose group(s) should be dissolved (any member pulls in the whole group)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_group_member_offset
tools.description: Reposition ONE grouped member relative to its group's anchor (the whole-unit lock's stage-2 numeric editor — PCBPanel's offset fields, MCP counterpart). A real change journals exactly one undoable step; resubmitting the same offset is a no-op reply (changed:false) and journals nothing. Refused (as an error) for an unknown component, a component not in a group, the group's own anchor (which has no editable offset), or a locked group. Reply: {component_id, group_id, dx_mm, dy_mm, changed}.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

component_id.description: Grouped, non-anchor component id to offset

dx_mm.description: X offset from the group anchor, in mm

dy_mm.description: Y offset from the group anchor, in mm

tools.name: minerva_pcb_get_layout_state
tools.description: Structured panel layout state, for verifying responsive UI behavior as data instead of screenshots. Returns {mode, width, sidebar_visible, drawer_open, view_menu_visible, properties_expanded, dock_position, plugin_build}. plugin_build is a hand-maintained deployed-script-vintage marker (not a git SHA, which is unavailable at runtime) — use it to tell which round's scripts a running panel is actually built from. Read-only — journals nothing.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_trace_width
tools.description: Set the width, in mm, of one existing trace. A real change journals exactly one undoable step and repaints the canvas live; re-setting the width the trace already has is a no-op reply (changed:false) and journals nothing. The reply reports the STORED width read back off the trace, not the requested one. Refused (as an error, with the model's own reason) for an unknown trace_id, a non-positive or non-finite width, or a width outside the 0.1-5.0 mm range this editor authors — widths are NOT clamped here, because this writes copper. Note the trace's clickable area follows its width, by design.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

trace_id.description: Trace id to re-width (as reported by minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry)

width_mm.description: New trace width in mm. Must be within 0.1-5.0; out-of-range values are refused, not clamped.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_list_vias
tools.description: List every VIA on the board — the plated holes that carry a net from one copper layer to another. Read-only; journals nothing. Returns a via_count plus one entry per via: {via_id, x_mm, y_mm, net_name, from_layer, to_layer, size_mm, drill_mm}. Use this to answer "which vias exist and where" without pulling the whole fabrication payload: minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry also carries a vias[] block, but that call walks every trace segment on the board and ABORTS entirely if any trace sits on a layer it cannot name, so an unrelated bad layer can make the via list unreadable. Both read the same board state, so the two never disagree. `via_id` is ABSENT (not blank) on a via restored from a board file predating stable via ids — such a via has no identity, so it cannot be deleted by id and cannot be selected on the canvas either. NOTE: minerva_pcb_add_via is NOT the counterpart of this tool — it edits a route-hint PROPOSAL, not the board, so nothing it adds appears here. Board vias are created by committing routes (minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints with commit, or minerva_pcb_import_trace_geometry); they are removed by minerva_pcb_delete_via or minerva_pcb_delete_traces' via_ids.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_delete_via
tools.description: Delete ONE board via by id. Exactly one journalled, undoable step — a single undo puts the via back. Get the id from minerva_pcb_list_vias (or from the `id` on each via in minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry). Returns {deleted, net_name, x_mm, y_mm, remaining_via_count}. An unknown via_id — including an empty one, which is what an id-less legacy via yields — is an ERROR, never a silent no-op: nothing is removed and nothing is journalled. This deletes the via ONLY; the traces meeting it are left exactly as they are, which can leave copper that changes layer with nothing connecting it, so check the routing afterwards. To remove several vias at once (or vias together with traces) in a single undo step, use minerva_pcb_delete_traces with via_ids instead. The human's Delete key, trash button and eraser on the canvas remove vias through this same model path and the same undo history.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

via_id.description: Via id to delete (as reported by minerva_pcb_list_vias)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_get_preference
tools.description: Read one PCB plugin preference. Plugin-scoped and persistent across app restarts; NOT a Minerva core preference. Returns {key, value, stored, default, description} plus min/max where the key is bounded — `stored` distinguishes "the user/agent actually chose this" from "never chosen, reading the default", which is what decides whether the preference is consulted at all. Read-only: journals nothing, writes nothing. An unknown key is an error that lists the keys that do exist. Known keys: trace_width_mm.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_preference
tools.description: Write one PCB plugin preference. Plugin-scoped, persisted under the plugin's data directory, survives app restart; NOT a Minerva core preference. The value is validated and CLAMPED to the key's declared range (unlike minerva_pcb_set_trace_width, which refuses out-of-range widths because it writes copper) and the reply reports the stored post-clamp value with {clamped, changed, applied_to_panel}. An unknown key is refused, never silently adopted. Setting trace_width_mm updates the live panel's trace-width box immediately and arms it for the next trace drawn. The arming is IMMEDIATE: the next trace drawn uses this width even on a board declaring design_rules.trace_width_mm. Board-rule precedence applies at seeding time only — on the next board load the declared rule wins again and the preference fills the no-rule case.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

value.description: New value. For trace_width_mm: width in mm, clamped into 0.1-5.0.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_validate
tools.description: Structurally validate a canonical PCB board (board-yaml contract). Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Returns {ok, errors:[{path,message}], warnings:[...]} — errors flag structural faults (missing required fields, duplicate refs, net pin refs that don't resolve, traces on unknown nets); warnings flag soft issues (out-of-bounds coordinates, trace narrower than design rules). Cheap: no geometry engine.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_generate
tools.description: Generate KiCad files from a canonical PCB board. Args {yaml|board, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. Returns {files:{'<name>.kicad_pcb':text, '<name>.kicad_sch':text, '<name>.kicad_pro':text}, written:[{path,bytes_written}]}. The .kicad_pcb faithfully carries components/pads/traces/outline/vias at the authored coordinates; .kicad_sch/.kicad_pro are minimal netlist-carrying skeletons. When out_dir is given the files are also written to disk.

name.description: Optional output file basename (defaults to board name).

out_dir.description: Optional directory to also write the files to.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_gerbers
tools.description: Generate fabrication files (Gerber RS-274X/X2 + Excellon drills) from a canonical PCB board — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml|board, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. Returns {files:{'<name>-F_Cu.gbr':text, ...}, written:[{path,bytes_written}], warnings:[...]}. NINE Gerber layers — F_Cu/B_Cu, F_Mask/B_Mask, F_Paste/B_Paste, F_SilkS/B_SilkS and Edge_Cuts — plus separate plated (PTH) and non-plated (NPTH) Excellon drill files (each drill file only when the board has holes of that class) and a '<name>-job.gbrjob' naming every layer's function. Coordinate format is self-declared per layer (read the %FS line, not assume 4.6). Silk is REAL footprint legend geometry plus stroke-font reference designators, on BOTH sides. Fab-correctness still needs a human viewer check — see docs/gerbers.md.

name.description: Optional output file basename (defaults to board name).

out_dir.description: Optional directory to also write the files to.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_drc
tools.description: Run a CONNECTIVITY/topology check over a canonical PCB board (pad centers + trace centerlines; NOT a geometric copper DRC — use minerva_pcb_drc_geometric for copper clearance/width/annular). Pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Returns {ok, findings:[{type,...}], counts:{type:count}}. Findings are structured and located: 'wrong_net_pad' (a trace endpoint on a different-net pad -> short) {net, at:[x,y], pad:{ref,pin,net}}; 'crossing' (two same-layer different-net traces that intersect, deduped per net-pair-per-layer) {nets:[a,b], layer, at}; 'dangling_endpoint' (a leaf trace endpoint reaching no pad/via/same-net copper -> open) {net, at}; 'layer_change_no_via' (a net's top and bottom copper meet with no via or through-hole pad -> missing via) {net, at}. T-junction taps and same-component internal-net pads are credited so they don't read as false opens. Scope: checks key off trace endpoints/segments — this is NOT a full ratsnest/connectivity check; a pad with no trace routed near it is not flagged as unrouted.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_drc_geometric
tools.description: Run a GEOMETRIC copper design-rule check over the ResolvedBoard IR — real pad/trace/via/hole copper geometry, pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Compiles the board to the ResolvedBoard IR, then checks GC1 min trace width, GC2 copper-copper clearance, GC3 drill/finished-hole (finished-hole is a necessary pre-DFM check — the IR carries drill diameter, not the plated finished bore), GC4 annular ring, GC5 copper-to-edge, GC6 hole-to-hole, GC7 filled-pour clearance, GC8 solder-mask sliver, GC10 hole-to-copper, and GC11 hole-to-edge (an unconditional containment refusal for a bore that crosses the outline or enters a cutout, plus a proximity check that runs only when the profile declares min_hole_to_edge_mm). GC9 silkscreen DFM (legend stroke width and legend-to-pad) is ADVISORY: its rows appear in a separate top-level `advisories` array and are counted, but are NOT in `findings` and NEVER change `verdict` — legend is cosmetic and is warned, never fatal. Floors declared OPTIONAL by a profile (hole-to-copper, hole-to-edge, the silk pair, feature-specific drill minima) are enforced only when that profile states them. `counts` reports ROWS, not check coverage: zero can mean either 'the profile stated no floor' or 'the check ran and found no row'. A GC9 failure is explicit as a counted `gc9_silk_indeterminate` advisory, never inferred from the two measuring counts. NEVER a false clean: modeled copper is exact or a superset (fail-safe), and unresolved/unsupported geometry FAILS CLOSED to an indeterminate result. Returns a discriminated union — determinate {ok:true, scope:'geometric', verifies_geometry:true, verdict:'clean'|'violations', board_id, source_digest, rule_profile, findings:[{type, entity_id, net_id, layer, measured_mm, required_mm, witness}], advisories:[...same shape...], counts, warnings} or indeterminate {ok:false, verdict:'indeterminate', error:{kind}} with NO clean/findings. Distinct from minerva_pcb_drc (connectivity/topology only). Corroborated against kicad-cli DRC.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_resolve
tools.description: Enrich a canonical PCB board with footprint silkscreen + courtyard graphics — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. For each component the footprint ref is resolved from the sha-verified seed library and its F.SilkS body outline + F.CrtYd keep-out graphics are attached as component['graphics'] (component-LOCAL coords; the placement/rotation transform stays the renderer's job, like pins). The existing inline pads are left untouched. FAIL-CLOSED coincidence guard: every declared pin's local position must equal the footprint pad's local position (matched by number) within 0.01mm, else {ok:false, error:{kind:'coincidence', ref, pin, delta_mm}} — never attach silk that would desync from the routed copper. Returns {ok, board:<resolved board>, stats:{components, silk_graphics, courtyard_graphics}}.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_normalize
tools.description: Rewrite a canonical PCB board to its normalized v2 shape — the sync-back the compile fold never persists on its own. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. For every pin carrying deprecated inline fabrication geometry (drill_mm/annulus_diameter_mm/pad_width_mm/pad_height_mm/plated): geometry REDUNDANT with the locked footprint pad is dropped, geometry that DIVERGES is migrated to a typed `override`, and an AMBIGUOUS pin (no matching footprint pad, or unverifiable) fail-closes the WHOLE normalize (better none than a half-normalized source). PURE — returns the normalized board for the host to persist; never writes to disk. Returns {ok:true, board:<normalized>, warnings:[{severity,code,message,...}]} on success (the warnings carry per-pin migrate/drop INFO diagnostics), or {ok:false, error:{kind:'normalize'|'parse', message, diagnostics}} on a fail-closed or parse fault. Idempotent: normalizing an already-normalized board is a no-op.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_check_libraries
tools.description: Verify component footprints against KiCAD footprint-library data. Args {yaml|board, lib_dir?:<path to a dir of *.pretty libs>}. With no lib_dir (the library data ships with a later child) returns {ok:true, checked:0, missing_data:true} — never a crash. With lib_dir returns {ok, checked, missing:[{ref,footprint,path}], missing_data:false}.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_check_bom
tools.description: Extract + validate a bill of materials from a canonical PCB board. Args {yaml|board, lib_dir?}. Returns {ok, items:[{refs,footprint,value,qty}], line_count, part_count, errors, warnings}. Warns on components missing a value or footprint. Footprint-presence flags are added only when lib_dir is supplied.

lib_dir.description: Optional KiCAD footprint-library dir for presence checks.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_stage
tools.description: Stage a .kicad_mod footprint into the WIP library layer, sha256-pinned and UNBLESSED. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName', kicad_mod_text, source_kind:'official_kicad|vendor_export|git|url|hand_authored|generated', source_ref, license, retrieved_at?, provenance_note?}. Returns {ref, entry:<acquisition-lock v2 entry with bless:null>, report:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}}. The text is PARSED FIRST â unparseable or padless input writes no file and mutates no lock. A staged entry cannot supply copper until minerva_pcb_footprint_bless records a verdict against it: unblessed refs are excluded from the resolution chain, so a board resolves the lower layer's part rather than the staged bytes. Re-staging a ref replaces its bytes and RESETS bless to null. Empty source_kind/source_ref/license are refused by name.

ref.description: Full footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName' — the library nickname names the .pretty directory the staged file is written into.

kicad_mod_text.description: The complete .kicad_mod s-expression text to stage.

source_kind.description: Provenance class: official_kicad, vendor_export, git, url, hand_authored or generated.

source_ref.description: Where the bytes came from (URL, git rev, datasheet + author, ...).

license.description: SPDX id or LicenseRef for the staged text.

provenance_note.description: Optional free-text note kept on the lock entry.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_report
tools.description: Render the two artifacts a human blesses a footprint against: a FACT TABLE and a self-contained SVG. Args {ref, max_svg_bytes?}. Returns {ref, facts:{ref, footprint_name, layer, source_kind, license, source_ref, pad_count, pad_numbers, pads:[{number,type,shape,x_mm,y_mm,size,drill,drill_shape,drill_size,layers,rotation,roundrect_rratio,solder_mask_margin,solder_paste_margin}], courtyard_bbox, body_bbox, assembly}, not_rendered:[{feature,detail,...}], svg, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256, svg_bytes, svg_truncated}. artifact_sha256 digests the staged content sha + the complete facts + not_rendered + the picture â it is what a human-tier bless must quote back as expected_artifact_sha256. Coordinates in facts are footprint-LOCAL with KiCad's y-DOWN sign (verbatim from the .kicad_mod); the SVG negates y so the picture is a conventional top view, and does not mirror x, so back-side geometry is drawn as seen through the board. not_rendered lists EVERY parsed element the picture omits â an empty not_rendered is the only condition under which the render shows the whole part. svg_sha256/svg_bytes always describe the WHOLE artifact even when svg itself is truncated for transport.

ref.description: Footprint ref to report on ('LibNick:PartName'); resolves through the layer chain, staged WIP parts included.

max_svg_bytes.description: Truncate the returned svg body at this many bytes (default 200000). svg_sha256/svg_bytes still describe the whole artifact.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_bless
tools.description: Record a bless verdict against a staged footprint, which is what lets it supply copper. Args {ref, verdict?:'approved'|'rejected', who?, blessed_at?, expected_artifact_sha256?}. Returns {ref, entry:<entry with bless:{tier, verdict, who, artifact_sha256, content_sha256, blessed_at}>, report:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}}. TIERING: source_kind official_kicad AUTO-BLESSES on provenance â omit verdict for it, and passing one is refused rather than silently recorded, so the lock can always distinguish parts a human reviewed from parts policy trusted. Every other source_kind (hand_authored above all â we authored those numbers) requires an explicit human verdict PLUS expected_artifact_sha256: the artifact_sha256 of the minerva_pcb_footprint_report the reviewer actually looked at. If the staged content changed since that review the bless REFUSES â an approval never transfers to an artifact nobody saw. The render is regenerated here and its digest pinned, so a footprint that cannot be rendered cannot be blessed. A 'rejected' verdict is recorded and keeps the ref unresolvable.

verdict.description: 'approved' or 'rejected'. OMIT for an official_kicad entry, which auto-blesses; supplying one for it is refused.

who.description: Who performed the rendered check. Required for a human-tier verdict.

blessed_at.description: Timestamp to record (defaults to UTC now).

expected_artifact_sha256.description: artifact_sha256 of the report the reviewer looked at. Required with a human-tier verdict; the bless refuses if the staged content renders a different artifact now.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_acquire_footprint
tools.description: Acquire ONE official KiCad footprint by ref and make it usable in a single call. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName'}. Performs outbound HTTPS to gitlab.com for the kicad-footprints file at the release tag pinned in pcb/libraries.lock.json (the lock is the single source of truth for which official release this plugin tracks â the tag is read, never restated here), then hands the bytes to the worker, which parse-validates them, stages them into the WIP library layer, and records the auto-tier verdict official_kicad provenance earns. Returns {ref, layer:'wip', sha256, source_ref:'kicad-footprints@<tag>/<Lib>.pretty/<Name>.kicad_mod', license, bless:{tier:'auto', verdict, who, artifact_sha256, blessed_at}, entry, report_summary:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}} â the ref resolves immediately afterwards. Refuses without writing anything on: a ref with a path separator or traversal segment, a non-200 status (404 = no such part at this release), a body over 1 MiB, non-UTF-8 bytes, or content that is markup rather than a footprint s-expression. The sha256 of the fetched bytes is recomputed independently worker-side and a mismatch is refused. ACQUISITION is the only library operation that needs a network: resolution reads sha-pinned bytes off disk and never opens a socket, so a fetch failure blocks adding this part and nothing else.

ref.description: Official KiCad footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName' (e.g. 'Resistor_SMD:R_0402_1005Metric') — the library nickname names the upstream .pretty directory.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_export_assembly
tools.description: Generate a pre-assembly order package (BOM CSV + CPL/pick-and-place CSV) from a canonical PCB board for one assembly house profile — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml|board, profile?:<house id, default "jlc">, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. "jlc" is the only house profile that currently offers assembly service; "oshpark" is a KNOWN house that refuses (bare-board only — no assembly service). Returns {profile, bom:{filename,rows,path}, cpl:{filename,rows,path}} — rows counts data rows (header excluded); path is omitted unless out_dir was given, in which case both CSVs are also written to disk. Refusals are NAMED, never a silent best-guess format or a blank identity cell: a component the profile requires identity for (jlc requires mpn) and lacks it refuses naming the component ref; an unrecognized or assembly-incapable house id refuses naming the id. CPL rotation is emitted verbatim from the authored rotation_deg (KiCad-equivalent clockwise convention); CPL Y is the authored y_mm negated, X verbatim. Calls the worker's assembly_bom then assembly_cpl methods over the same board+profile — whichever refuses first is the error this tool surfaces.

profile.description: Assembly house profile id (default "jlc" — the only assembly-capable profile shipped; "oshpark" is known but refuses — bare-board only).

out_dir.description: Optional directory to also write the files to.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries
tools.description: Fetch the curated KiCAD symbol/footprint library subset (pcb/libraries.lock.json) that minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom read. Downloads each locked entry, verifies it by sha256, and skips entries already present+verified (safe to re-run). Args: none. Returns {tag, fetched:[names], skipped:[names], failed:[{name,reason}]}. Requires network access; never partially writes a corrupted/mismatched file (atomic temp+rename, reject on sha mismatch). Run this once (or after refreshing pcb/libraries.lock.json) before relying on real footprint/symbol checks — see minerva_pcb_library_status to check what's already fetched.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_library_status
tools.description: Report whether the KiCAD library-data subset (pcb/libraries.lock.json) has been fetched and verified. Args: none. Returns {present, version_tag, entries_verified, total_entries, missing:[names]}. present:false (or a non-empty missing[]) means minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom will report missing_data:true — run minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries to fix. Never fails: an absent lock file or data directory reports present:false rather than erroring.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_propose
tools.description: Route the open route hints into the ROUTING WORKSPACE as candidates (ghost routes), writing no proposal annotations. The workspace-native replacement for minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints' propose half: candidates carry exact per-segment layers/widths and vias, stable ids, and a disposition (proposed/pinned/superseded/rejected/committed) you act on with the other minerva_pcb_workspace_* verbs. Args {editor_name, hint_ids?}. Returns {proposed, candidates:[{candidate_id, task_id, net, generation, disposition, validation, segment_count, via_count, layers, bend_count, routed_length_mm, length_ratio?, misalignment_mm?}], holds, routes_returned, unrouted, stuck, drc_summary, drc_geometric_summary, board_health, stale_candidate_ids, island_deltas?} — board_health (DCR 019fd5fd9084) is the worker's whole-board completeness + assembly advisory {complete, missing_copper, partial, assembly:{status, findings}, approximate:true}, enriched panel-side with board_revision and preflight.rendered_this_revision. ROUTE QUALITY (Epoch UX2 station 4 + HITL-6): every candidate record carries bend_count and routed_length_mm (zeros for a vias-only candidate), plus length_ratio (routed / per-run manhattan minimum, approximate; absent when that minimum is ~0) and, on single-run candidates, misalignment_mm — the perpendicular offset between the span's endpoints (min(|dx|,|dy|)). THE 2-PIN RULE: on a two-pin span, ANY bend means the pads do not align — length_ratio 1.0 only says the detour is efficient, never that it is necessary; misalignment_mm > 0 says the PLACEMENT is the thing to fix (align with minerva_pcb_move_component snap_to_grid:false, then re-propose) — weigh that before committing. A high ratio or bend count on a longer hop is the same smell at larger scale. HOLDS: a task whose current candidate is PINNED is HELD — the incoming candidate is NOT created and the pin stands, so candidates[] is SHORTER than routes_returned; holds[] names {task_id, held_candidate_id, net, reason} for each. Unpin or reject that candidate (or minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route it) to replace it. Per-component emitter capability notes now ride `emitter_notes` (when non-empty); stuck[] is unrouted pad pairs plus per-hint routing warnings only. TASK CONSTRAINTS ARE CONSUMED (Epoch UX1 station 9, DCR 019fd095e694): a selected hint whose task carries a routing_constraint (minted by minerva_pcb_add_route_intent's corridor arg, or by a prior minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route corridor/preserve_shape_as_corridor) steers THIS proposal's router run — the stored corridor overrides that hint's own legacy waypoints, if it even has any. Every candidate a constraint steered carries an additive `constraint_revision` key naming which revision produced it. LEGACY MIGRATION (Epoch UX1 station 12): a selected non-'detailed' hint carrying inline waypoints whose task has no routing_constraint yet has that corridor seeded ONCE into a durable task constraint (authored_by "migration") before this run, and the hint's waypoints are then marked superseded and refuse further edits.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_commit
tools.description: COMMIT route candidates (the DCR's Accept): exact geometry becomes REAL COPPER on the board — contiguous same-layer/-width segments chain into ONE polyline trace each (docket 019fce6184c2), plus vias — and each candidate becomes 'committed', in ONE UNDOABLE STEP. Pass EXACTLY ONE of candidate_id (single) or candidate_ids (BATCH, docket 019fd0ab6dd2). A batch is one history entry and ONE undo reverting every member's copper and disposition together, and each member's validation_at_commit is its PRE-batch verdict — sequential single commits would mark clean batch-mates stale purely from the sibling's own revision bump. Single form returns {candidate_id, task_id, task_state, trace_ids, via_ids, consumed_hint_ids, validation_at_commit, candidate, stale_candidate_ids}; batch form returns {results:[per-member], committed_count, trace_ids, via_ids, candidates, stale_candidate_ids}. Source hints are CONSUMED BY RECORD, not deleted. ALL validation precedes ALL mutation across the WHOLE batch: any refusal (illegal transition, unmodelable geometry, duplicate id) leaves the board, dispositions and history untouched and names the offending candidate. Committing an unchecked or violating candidate is allowed and reported, never silently blessed. PLACEMENT ACKNOWLEDGMENT GATE (DCR 019fd5fd9084): when the panel's cached assembly state is FRESH (same board_revision), carries status 'findings', and at least one finding's components intersect the committing candidate's own endpoint components, the commit REFUSES with error 'placement_blocker_unacknowledged' listing blocking_findings — pass acknowledge_placement:true to commit anyway (the reply then records acknowledged_placement_findings). Known findings at the commit point require explicit acknowledgment; a STALE/absent cache or an 'indeterminate' assembly state never blocks — the reply just carries an advisory assembly_note. In a batch, one unacknowledged blocked member refuses the WHOLE batch (all-or-nothing, checked before any copper).

acknowledge_placement.description: Set true to commit THROUGH a fresh assembly 'findings' state whose findings touch this candidate's endpoint components — without it such a commit refuses placement_blocker_unacknowledged. tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route
tools.description: TRY AGAIN on a whole route: re-run the router scoped to this candidate's own source hints and land a NEW generation for the same task. Args {editor_name, candidate_id, corridor?, preserve_shape_as_corridor?, clear_constraint?, width_mm?, expected_constraint_revision?}. WIDTH (Epoch UX2 station 3): `width_mm` writes the new trace width onto every source hint's kind_payload before the router runs — a durable review-time width change (the reply echoes width_mm; candidates carry width_source:"hint"), landing whether or not the router leg succeeds, and undoable per hint via the hint revision stack. Returns the propose-shaped reply plus {rerouted_candidate_id, prior_task_id, same_task}. The router runs FIRST and the prior candidate is retired only after it answers, so a routing failure never leaves the task with no answer at all. Refused by name when the candidate has already left the live set, or when it carries no source route-hint provenance (no_source_hints) — the panel's router bridge can only scope a run by hint selection today, so an unaddressable reroute would silently become a whole-board run. STEERING (Epoch UX1 station 9, DCR 019fd095e694, docket 019fd057ea0b comment 1028): `corridor` (Array of {x_mm,y_mm}) REPLACES the candidate's task's durable routing_constraint with this corridor, bumping its revision; `preserve_shape_as_corridor` (bool) DERIVES that new corridor from the candidate's OWN current geometry instead, before this same call reroutes it away — the visible alternative to a hidden 'promote edit to steering' verb. The two are mutually exclusive BY PRESENCE (refused corridor_args_conflict if both keys are sent). CLEARING (Epoch UX2 station 2): `clear_constraint:true` REMOVES the task's routing_constraint — this reroute runs unguided, the owner hint's supersession marker is stripped, and every reply carries cleared_constraint_revision. An intent-shape hint (no waypoints) then stays unguided on every later propose; a hint that DOES carry its own waypoints re-takes authority instead — the next propose re-seeds a corridor from them (station-12 legacy seeding), at a revision above the cleared one (revisions stay monotonic across clears, so stale pre-clear candidates never pass the commit gate). Mutually exclusive (when true) with corridor/preserve_shape_as_corridor; refused no_constraint_to_clear by name on an unconstrained task; expected_constraint_revision guards a clear the same way it guards a steer. `expected_constraint_revision` (int; 0 for an unconstrained task) is optimistic concurrency on the task's constraint — a mismatch refuses constraint_revision_conflict naming the actual revision and steers nothing. preserve_shape_as_corridor is refused multi_span_task when the candidate's task answers more than one hint (no single owner for the derived corridor), and no_single_path when the candidate's own geometry is more than one disconnected run (it is never bridged with a fabricated jump); an explicit corridor:[] is refused corridor_present_but_empty. ALL of these preconditions — candidate exists, its disposition can still reach superseded, its source hints are still present, and (when steering) the task/revision/corridor checks above — are checked BEFORE anything is written. DURABILITY: only once every precondition has passed is the constraint written, BEFORE the router runs — a router failure after that point (worker unavailable, etc.) leaves the bumped constraint standing rather than undoing it, and the failure reply says so: it carries `steered:true` and the NEW `constraint_revision` so the bump is never silent — pass that revision, not whatever you read before this call, as expected_constraint_revision on a retry.

corridor.description: Replaces the candidate's task routing_constraint with this corridor before rerouting (bumps its revision). Mutually exclusive with preserve_shape_as_corridor by presence.

Mutually exclusive (when true) with corridor and preserve_shape_as_corridor. Refuses no_constraint_to_clear on an unconstrained task.

expected_constraint_revision.description: Optimistic concurrency: the task's constraint_revision you last read (0 if the task was unconstrained). A mismatch refuses constraint_revision_conflict rather than steering. Only consulted when corridor or preserve_shape_as_corridor:true is also given.

The routing engine scopes by WHOLE NET and refuses a span outright rather than widening it, so span-scoped replacement geometry cannot be obtained; this verb therefore reroutes the ENTIRE route and stamps {degraded:true, degraded_to:"whole_route", requested_segment_ids, limitation, limitation_docket:"019fc155bc32"} on the reply. It deliberately creates NO span-scoped task: recording a span question whose answer is whole-route geometry would make the model claim a scope it never had. Use minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route directly if a whole-route reroute is what you meant.

tools.description: SET-SCOPED draft DRC over route candidates: runs the DRC rules over the UNION of the board's committed copper and every checked candidate's draft copper, so a collision between two candidates, or between a candidate and real copper, is found. Args {editor_name, candidate_ids?, include_stale?}. Omit candidate_ids to check every live candidate. Returns {checked, checked_stale, per_candidate:{candidate_id: clean|violating|error}, findings, validation, board_token, workspace_generation, newly_stale_candidate_ids}. Findings name SUBJECT IDENTITY — subjects:[{candidate_id, segment_id|via_id}] — not just a net, so a violation points at the exact ghost segment or via. STALE CANDIDATES REFUSE: the workspace is rebased onto the live board revision first, and a candidate generated against a different revision (or invalidated by a verb) comes back as error "stale_candidates" rather than a verdict. Two exits, both named in the refusal: reroute/re-propose it for geometry against THIS board, or re-run with include_stale:true to check the existing geometry deliberately.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_route_bus_direct
tools.description: Draw a parallel bus of real copper directly (campaign 2 epoch C unit 5, DCR 019fb572b888) — the MCP parity tool for the canvas Bus tool, calling the SAME validation path and the SAME single-journal-step commit. Takes an ORDERED list of already-declared net names (order is preserved verbatim — never re-sorted, which is what lets a human pick 'the I2S trio' in a specific order and get one net per track in that order) and a spine polyline; emits one parallel Trace per net, offset from the spine at clearance-or-better pitch (each net's width auto-derives from its widest EXISTING trace, else the board default, unless width_override is given), mitered through bends so pitch stays constant. Needs 2+ nets and a 2+ point spine after duplicate points are dropped. REFUSES (never commits self-overlapping copper) when any spine segment is shorter than the widest per-net offset — the inner track would fold back on itself; the error names the offending segment and offset. All N traces land in ONE undoable history step: Ctrl+Z (or PCBData.undo) removes every trace this call created. Returns {trace_ids, nets, widths, layer, undo_note} or a named error. Example call: {"editor_name": "PCB1", "nets": ["I2S_BCLK", "I2S_LRCLK", "I2S_DATA"], "points": [{"x_mm": 10, "y_mm": 10}, {"x_mm": 30, "y_mm": 10}, {"x_mm": 30, "y_mm": 30}], "layer": "top"}.

NOTHING is journalled and the board is not mutated — resolve each candidate with minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/_reject/pin, or the canvas candidate menu. The canvas gesture's Shift+Enter calls the SAME bus_propose_plan, so agent and human propose identical geometry by construction. Re-proposing the same bus supersedes the prior ghost per net; a net whose current candidate is PINNED is HELD (candidate not created, named in holds[]), same as minerva_pcb_workspace_propose. Returns {proposed, candidates:[{candidate_id, task_id, net, generation, disposition, validation, segment_count, via_count, layers, bend_count, routed_length_mm, length_ratio?, misalignment_mm?}], holds, nets, widths, layer} or a named error.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_route_intent
tools.description: Author a ROUTE INTENT — connectivity between two pins, no routing performed (Epoch UX1 station 8, DCR 019fd095e694). Atomically creates: (a) a pcb_route_hint annotation carrying ONLY source_pin/dest_pin/note — waypoints is always empty; the corridor NEVER lands on this object. (b) an eagerly-created RouteTask in the routing workspace (task_id "NET|hint_id"): a later propose of THIS hint alone reuses that same task, and a propose that merges this intent's route with another open intent's on the same net (one worker-attributed answer naming both hint ids) ABSORBS both eager tasks into the merged one — carrying over a solitary routing_constraint; two CONFLICTING constraints are KEPT on their surviving singleton tasks (each keeps steering its own hint per-hint, the merged task stays unconstrained, and the conflict is surfaced as constraint_conflicts — Codex 1047 P1-A) — rather than orphaning either eager task or minting a third (cold review H3-1). (c) when `corridor` is given, a routing_constraint stored ON THE TASK ({corridor_points, revision:1, authored_by:"ai", base_board_revision}) — durable steering with one authoritative home, distinct from the connectivity annotation. minerva_pcb_workspace_propose CONSUMES this constraint (Epoch UX1 station 9): it steers that proposal's router run and the landed candidate carries the constraint_revision that produced it. source_pin and dest_pin must already share exactly one net (connect them first with minerva_pcb_connect_net otherwise). Deleting the intent annotation before it is answered cascades: its still-candidate-less eager task is dropped too (a task any candidate has landed on is left alone). Optional `width_mm` (Epoch UX2 station 3) lands on the minted hint's kind_payload — the durable width channel the router already honors (candidates carry width_mm + width_source:"hint") — so trace width is stated WITH the intent instead of patched onto the annotation afterwards; invalid values refuse invalid_width. Returns {success, hint_id, task_id, net, ref?, constraint_revision?, width_mm?, note} where note names the legal next step (minerva_pcb_workspace_propose or minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints with hint_ids:[hint_id]), or a named refusal: pin_unresolvable, cross_net_pins, single_endpoint_only, workspace_unavailable, annotation_rejected. AUTHOR CORRIDORS FROM REAL BOARD CONTEXT (HITL-4): pin coordinates alone do not show footprint bodies, courtyards, or existing copper — read minerva_pcb_get_image / minerva_pcb_spatial_query / minerva_pcb_describe_component (and heed board_health / the load reply's assembly state) BEFORE choosing corridor points, and settle open placement questions before proposing copper through them.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

dest_pin.description: Destination pin ref "Component.Pin", e.g. "D1.2". Must resolve to the SAME net as source_pin.

note.description: Optional discussion text carried on the intent annotation.

width_mm.description: Optional trace width in mm for routes answering this intent — written to the hint's kind_payload.width_mm (candidates report width_source:"hint"). Positive number; omit for the net class default.

corridor.description: Optional initial steering corridor, board mm, in order. Stored on the eagerly-created RouteTask's routing_constraint (revision 1) — never on the intent annotation. Read by minerva_pcb_workspace_propose and minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route (Epoch UX1 station 9): a selected hint whose task carries this constraint has it override the hint's own waypoints for that router run, and the landed candidate cites the constraint's revision. An EXPLICITLY EMPTY array (corridor: []) is refused ("corridor present but empty") rather than silently treated as "no corridor" — omit the key entirely for that.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_edit_candidate
tools.description: Edit ONE candidate's own geometry — the ONE discriminated candidate-edit verb (Epoch UX1 station 10, DCR 019fd095e694, docket 019fd057ea0b comments 1026/1028). EDIT != POLICY: this touches only the named candidate — never its task, never its routing_constraint — and it does NOT pin. To make an edited shape survive the next re-propose, reroute with minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route's preserve_shape_as_corridor:true instead; to hold this exact candidate against a batch re-propose, pin it explicitly (minerva_pcb_workspace_pin). Args {editor_name, candidate_id, op, expected_candidate_revision?, …op args}. op == "move_junction" (args point:[x_mm,y_mm], to:[x_mm,y_mm]): junction IDENTITY, not a flattened bend index — a candidate can carry ≥2 DISCONNECTED copper paths (INV-3), and a bend is commonly the shared endpoint of multiple segment ids, so every segment endpoint AND every via coincident with point (within the same tight epsilon the segment graph's own adjacency test uses) moves atomically to to. Refused BY NAME: junction_not_found (nothing coincident with point), ambiguous_junction (point matches junctions on more than one of this candidate's disconnected paths — move each path's junction separately, or supply a point that identifies only one), degenerate_result (the move would collapse a segment to zero length — never emitted, docket 019f9cc3245d). Moving a route's TERMINAL endpoint (the end that anchors a pad on a real board) is an ALLOWED edit, not refused — it detaches the draft's copper from that pad, but this candidate's staled validation and bumped candidate_revision are exactly what a subsequent check/commit exists to report, not a gap this tool needs to close itself. op == "insert_via" (args position:[x_mm,y_mm], from_layer, to_layer): DELEGATES verbatim to the existing RoutingWorkspace.add_via — the path-scoped via/layer edit entry INV-3 names, not reimplemented. Its own named refusals (illegal_via_span, no_segment_at_point, degenerate_insert_at_endpoint, degenerate_insert_on_via, segment_locked, from_layer_mismatch) pass through unchanged. CONCURRENCY (symmetric with station 9's expected_constraint_revision): expected_candidate_revision, when given, is checked against the candidate's CURRENT candidate_revision BEFORE either op runs — a mismatch refuses candidate_revision_conflict {candidate_id, expected_candidate_revision, actual_candidate_revision} and mutates nothing; a successful edit bumps candidate_revision and the reply reports the new one — chain a second edit with THAT number, not whatever was read before this call. Both ops refuse a TERMINAL candidate (committed/rejected/superseded) by name (candidate_not_editable) — a terminal candidate is a record, not a draft.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

op.description: Which candidate-local geometry edit to perform.

point.description: move_junction only: [x_mm, y_mm] — the junction's CURRENT position. Every segment endpoint and via coincident with this point, on ONE connected path, moves atomically.

to.description: move_junction only: [x_mm, y_mm] — where the junction moves to.

position.description: insert_via only: [x_mm, y_mm] — where to split a segment and insert a via. Delegates verbatim to RoutingWorkspace.add_via.

from_layer.description: insert_via only: the layer the copper AT position is actually on — a mismatch is refused (from_layer_mismatch), never silently corrected.

to_layer.description: insert_via only: the layer the via's downstream run flips to.

expected_candidate_revision.description: Optimistic concurrency: the candidate_revision you last read. A mismatch refuses candidate_revision_conflict rather than editing anything.

skills.title: PCB design (IR-compiled, fail-closed DRC/routing/CAM)
skills.summary: Sole PCB surface (the in-tree editor and .minpcb are retired; boards are .pcbskel documents). Author canonical YAML (docs/board-yaml.md) or place parts with minerva_pcb_add_component/minerva_pcb_connect_net, then load with minerva_pcb_load_board. minerva_pcb_validate checks structure; minerva_pcb_drc checks net connectivity; minerva_pcb_drc_geometric compiles to the ResolvedBoard IR and checks real copper (width, clearance, drill, annular ring, edge, hole spacing) — fail-closed, so 'indeterminate' is not a pass. Routing is IR-native and fail-closed too: author pcb_route_hint annotations, run minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints (or minerva_pcb_workspace_propose) to land RouteCandidates in the routing workspace, then resolve each with minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/minerva_pcb_workspace_reject. minerva_pcb_generate emits KiCad text; minerva_pcb_gerbers emits Gerber+Excellon output — both resolve footprints from a locked seed library and fail closed rather than approximate copper. minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom check parts against a separate KiCAD subset minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries downloads.
skills.preconditions: A PCB editor tab is open (minerva_list_editors) or spawned via minerva_create_plugin_editor (editor_item_id "new_pcb"); the board-YAML tools (validate/generate/gerbers/drc/drc_geometric/check_libraries/check_bom) take board text directly and need no open editor.
skills.outcome: The board renders with real components, nets and routed copper; minerva_pcb_validate and both DRC tools report clean or name exactly what is wrong and where; minerva_pcb_gerbers/minerva_pcb_generate produce fabrication files traceable to the same footprint geometry DRC checked; route proposals are inspectable before they become copper.
skills.steps:
1. Open the editor tab (minerva_list_editors) or create one (minerva_create_plugin_editor, editor_item_id "new_pcb").
2. Author canonical YAML or place parts with minerva_pcb_add_component/minerva_pcb_connect_net, then minerva_pcb_load_board.
3. Validate with minerva_pcb_validate; check minerva_pcb_library_status once (minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries if needed), then minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom.
4. Route: add pcb_route_hint annotations (minerva_annotations_add), minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints (commit=false) or minerva_pcb_workspace_propose to land candidates, then minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/minerva_pcb_workspace_reject each candidate_id — or re-run apply_route_hints with commit=true.
5. Run minerva_pcb_drc and minerva_pcb_drc_geometric on the finished board; 'indeterminate' blocks, it is not a pass.
6. Export with minerva_pcb_generate and minerva_pcb_gerbers; a human must still eyeball the output before real fabrication.
skills.system_prompt: Sole PCB surface; the legacy in-tree editor is gone. Routing, DRC and CAM share one ResolvedBoard IR compiler and one rule: canvas may degrade, but routing/DRC/CAM never approximate copper — unresolvable geometry fails closed. minerva_pcb_drc is connectivity-only; minerva_pcb_drc_geometric is the real copper check and must pass before fabrication. minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints always proposes before it commits. minerva_pcb_resolve exposes resolved silk/courtyard geometry directly (compile already does this internally for gerbers/generate/drc_geometric); minerva_pcb_normalize migrates legacy inline pin geometry to the current schema.
